aliasRule: Internal decision keys are normalized at the host boundary and cannot appear in public DomainDetailCode. An unknown internal key is refused; retired dead codes have no alias. THIS MAP IS CONTEXT-FREE, so only a key whose public detail is the same at EVERY originating boundary may appear here. Two classes of key deliberately do NOT: an ORIGIN-DEPENDENT key, whose detail differs by actor - native.requested-capability-unregistered is CONFIG.INVALID when a user configured it and carries no detail when the host produced it - cannot be expressed by a context-free pair, and its derivation is the origin-aware route registry named in each selector; and a key whose DomainDetail is lawfully ABSENT never surfaces as a DomainDetailCode and so needs no alias, its internal key being retained in the operational diagnostic record instead. Absence of an alias is therefore a positive statement about a key, not an omission.
newInThisCorrection: Four DomainDetailCode members were added because the CommandEnvelope failure branch REQUIRES a nonempty errors array of DomainDetail, and four of the capability/Coverage routes had no code that named their remedy. Reuse was preferred wherever it was honest - external configuration keeps CONFIG.INVALID and a NOT-SELECTED cell keeps PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED - and these four were added rather than borrowing an unrelated remedy: `a supplied spec names an unregistered capability`, `the installed release declaration is malformed`, `the provider emitted an unsupported deficiency/cause pair` and `the host violated its own invariant` are four different things for a caller to do next.
scopeBindingDetailsRegistered: TWO EXISTING EMISSIONS WERE REGISTERED, and nothing new was invented. workflows_model.verify_scope_parameter_binding has always raised REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with BASELINE.SCOPE_NOT_A_SELECTED_PARAMETER and with BASELINE.SCOPE_PARAMETER_DIGEST_MISMATCH, and neither name was a member of this registry, of the mirrored DomainDetailCode enum, or of internalAliases - so the REAL public carrier (workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/StepTermination) REFUSED both terminations and the two refusals had no public route at all. They are registered here rather than renamed, because the emitting code, the owning normative prose (identity-and-evidence.md, `Where the binding is actually decided, and where it is only asserted`) and the existing controls all already use these exact names, and because the two conditions are DIFFERENT things for a caller to do next: NOT_A_SELECTED_PARAMETER says the analysis spec selects no ScopeDocumentV1 parameter at all - state one, or stop asking to be bound to a scope policy - while DIGEST_MISMATCH says exactly one IS selected and the supplied document is not it - supply the selected document. Collapsing them onto one existing code would delete that distinction and silently rename two published outputs. They are NOT internalAliases entries: an alias maps an internal decision key that may not appear as a public DomainDetailCode, and these two are emitted directly into the DomainDetail.code position by their own owner. The AMBIGUOUS selection introduced by the same correction keeps CONFIG.INVALID and is unchanged: it was already registered and no third BASELINE.SCOPE_* spelling is created. No D9 class, error code, exit code, faultCause, remedy string or reachability changes.
